task_summary: Modernized BukSU Capstone Team invitation workflow into a high-capacity bulk invitation engine adhering to /i-arrange and /i-bolder: 1) Created BulkInviteModal with dual inviting modalities (interactive debounced section search & regex-powered comma/space/newline email parser). 2) Integrated real-time capacity tracking (1 leader + up to 3 invitees, hard-capped at MAX_TEAM_MEMBERS = 4). 3) Built staged candidate tray with dismissible chips and real-time eligibility tags (blocking warnings, cross-section alerts). 4) Built backend bulk invitation endpoint (POST /api/teams/:id/bulk-invite), Zod schema, service capacity checks, 6-digit code generation, and structured batch results. 5) Upgraded CreateTeamForm with staged teammate chips and StudentTeamDetail with hero invite banner and multi-code copy. Passed 9/9 client targeted unit tests, 27/27 server integration tests, 208/189 endpoint parity (UNMATCHED_COUNT=0), 60/60 agentic validation checks, clean governance pipeline, and 10-point Playwright visual audit across desktop and mobile in light and dark themes.
lessons_learned: Lesson: BukSU Capstone Phase 0 teams enforce a strict 4-member maximum (1 leader + up to 3 members). Bulk invitation UI must calculate remaining available slots dynamically against both active members and unexpired pending invites to prevent over-allocation.

Prevention: When providing power-user paste inputs for student emails, use flexible regex parsing (/[,;\s\n]+/) combined with RFC 5322 email validation and deduplication against existing team members and pending invites before dispatching batch API requests.

Runbook / Checklist for Bulk Operations: 1. Validate batch payload size with Zod (min 1, max available slots). 2. Ensure atomic or structured batch outcome reporting (succeeded, failed, reused) with per-candidate error messaging. 3. Provide copy-to-clipboard for generated batch artifacts (such as 6-digit invite codes). 4. Maintain backward compatibility for single-entity forms.
